thread:
maria: quick alert — long-run kv-cache playback (40k tokens) on our rtx6000 pool shows unbounded GPU memory climb. attaching summary and repro steps.

jia: can you drop the exact command, model revision and runtime SHA?

maria: repro steps: 
```
# env: runtime@feature/kvcache-remap-fix
python tools/repro_long_playback.py --model gpt-7b --seq 40000 --batch 1 --device rtx6000
```
observed: KV pager keeps increasing mapped pages instead of stabilizing after warmup. sample journal: 
```
[KV_PAGER] total_pages=1380 active_pages=1354 mapped_slots=1380
[KV_PT] entries=34500 live_refs=34500
GPU mem: 13020MiB -> 15560MiB -> 18010MiB (steady increase over 2h)
```
Seems similar to a stale mapping left behind after a cross-device remap. repro on rtx6000 and 3080; A100 baseline does not repro.

oliver: interesting — consumer GPUs don't run MPS in our infra, so code paths differ. Did you try with KV_BIND_TO_GPU or CUDA IPC toggles? Also capture kv tracer.

maria: traced events (excerpt):
```
{\"t\":211, \"op\":\"evict\", \"slot\":2047, \"from_dev\":0}
{\"t\":212, \"op\":\"remap\", \"slot\":2047, \"to_dev\":1}
{\"t\":213, \"op\":\"reclaim\", \"slot\":2047, \"success\":false}
```
The reclaim fails because the slot's refcount appears nonzero after remap. hypothesis: remap sets the owner but does not always clear previous owner's metadata (flags/refcount), leaving a stale pinned/refcount state. On some GPUs the memory ordering or the async memcpy bailout triggers early returns that leave page_meta.in_use true.

raman: past bug we've seen: `memcpy_async` error path can exit without clearing PAGE_PINNED; check `kvcache/evict.cpp:release_slot` and `page_table.cpp:remap_slot` ordering and atomicity.

raman: local quick patch to test:
```diff
- page_meta[slot].owner = new_dev;
+ // ensure atomic swap of owner and clear pinned to avoid stale retention
+ old = atomic_exchange(&page_meta[slot].owner, new_dev);
+ atomic_and(&page_meta[slot].flags, ~PAGE_FLAG_PINNED);
```

samir: run this on H100/A100/RTX please — adding atomics in hot path could affect token latency.

maria: results: RTX6000: leak stopped; mapped_slots plateau. 3080: similar. A100: still stable (no regression pre-patch). H100 queued in CI.

qa: let's add a unit/regression test: `eng-runtime/tests/test_kv_reclaim_flaky.py` that runs ~10k tokens and asserts mapped_slots < 2000. Add flaky marker and increased iterations so CI will catch rare races.

maria: added test locally and saw 1/300 failure without patch; with patch 0/500 in local runs. Repro case involves concurrent cross-device remap while background batch flush is reclaiming — low frequency race.

oliver: good catch. also propose adding a CHECK in page_table shutdown to assert no owners remain: `CHECK(std::all_of(..., [](meta){ return meta.owner == -1; }))` — will trip in CI if not cleaned.

infra-bot: canary rollout: image `kvcache-remap-1977-canary` deployed to rtx6000 pool. Monitoring memory and eviction metrics for 4h.

raman: PR opened w/ patch, added atomic ops + tracer improvements + test: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-runtime/pull/4368 (draft). Pushed microbench numbers: token latency p50 baseline 4.7ms -> patched 4.9ms, p95 unchanged. CPU overhead minor.

samir: plan: once merged, run `perf/kv_pagemap_longctx` microbench on A100/H100/RTX to ensure no regression on throughput. Add perf job to perma-bench board.

maria: CI H100 results in progress — initial run looks OK but extended run scheduled overnight.

qa: labelled test flaky and set up rerun-on-fail for 24h. Also added note to not promote to main until H100 gating passes.

maria: artifact bundle stored at /artifacts/kv_remap/1977654321/ (tracers, logs, `kv_stats.json`).

infra-bot: canary status after 4h: healthy. mem_growth_rate=0.01%/hr, evictions_success=99.995%.

oliver: follow-up: investigate `cudaMemAdvise` and faster cross-dev remap strategies to reduce mmap churn on consumer cards. Could be a performance win.

maria: assigning follow-ups to @oliver and @raman for finalizing patch, H100 verification and backport to dedicated branch. Will reopen if infra-bot alerts. Thanks everyone :rocket:
